works.title:
Heritage
Ceramic Collection
works.desc:
Gorbon

Gorbon is one of Türkiye's longest-established ceramic brands. I had known the company for two generations, and when the third generation took over, that long relationship became the starting point for the Heritage Collection.

We laid out forty years of Gorbon production and selected thirty forms from the archive. I reduced each one to its essential geometry, redrew the proportions so the pieces related to one another, and applied a new shared colour palette. The collection is built from Gorbon's own history, but designed as a new family rather than a reproduction of the past.

works.title: Centerpieces
works.desc:
Armaggan

Between 2007 and 2010, I designed close to one hundred products that together helped establish Armaggan's identity. The collection consisted mainly of centrepieces and objects combining precious materials such as silver and marble with glass, porcelain and wood.

The work drew on cultural memory without relying on literal references. Its character came from proportion, material contrast and demanding craft detail. Many pieces required close work with specialist makers, bringing traditional techniques into a contemporary product language.

works.title: Studio Furniture Collection
works.desc:
Duduu

Dudu was founded as a collaborative initiative by a group of designers producing their own work. For the collective, I explored a simple question: how can furniture feel distinctly modern without becoming cold or unfamiliar?

The collection also questioned how much a product family should prescribe the room around it. The pieces share a clear relationship, but were never intended to create a complete “total look.” Each has enough character to stand on its own, while leaving room for other furniture, objects and the life already present in a home.
